payload.text: ST0031/04's close-out and dc's five run drivers are held under hv's two rulings of 10 Nov, both first-hand in dc's own window: "Hold until C5B9WJ is green, don't ship it unrun", and then, on being told the arms cannot reach the engine at all, "write the driver for exec_create_space before the cut." Recorded as utilz-vc's decisions 96 and 97. THE FIRST CONDITION IS MET: the arms ran GREEN in slot NTVCDH at head 5d7bfe37, plan_test 240 passed 0 failed and arngz.bats TAP 1..158 with 158 ok, 0 not ok, 0 skip, 0 todo, every count derived from the run, which is the first execution of any of ST0032. C5B9WJ itself was never granted and is denied naming NTVCDH as its supersession, its pin bf6e5f08 having gone stale by eight commits. RELEASED WHEN BOTH: ST0033's driver is proven, each arm seen red under its own mutation and green without, which is ST0033's AC-01.3; and hv has NAMED THE CUT'S HEAD, which hv has not. 5d7bfe37 is the arms' head and not the cut's, so the drivers stay void and unpinned. THE GREEN'S PATH SET, which replaces this hold's earlier and looser wording: "nothing outside intent/ has moved" was right only while the tree was gaining records, and it stopped being true the moment engine_test.lua appeared. What the arms actually read is opt/arngz/lib/plan.lua, opt/arngz/lib/arngz.lua, opt/arngz/test/plan_test.lua, opt/arngz/test/arngz.bats and opt/arngz/arngz, and those are what must not move for a green to go on describing the code it was taken on. As things stand: the ENGINE is untouched, arngz.lua and plan.lua byte-identical to the green, which is the half that matters; plan_test.lua and opt/arngz/arngz unmoved; and arngz.bats is one 13-line deletion different, lua_bin having moved to opt/utilz/test/test_helper.bash as a Highlander fix that vc ruled to keep, with its mode bit restored to 100755 after an editor lost it. The suite also gains engine.bats and engine_test.lua. So arngz.bats's 158 want re-running at the cut, which a cut does anyway, and which ST0032's sixteen ATs want regardless since every one is still awaiting a verdict.
